Condition: The Q3 2026 access review did not cover the source code repository, although the ticket said all systems were reviewed
Root cause: No written system checklist. The review list is kept in the IT Manager's notes and does not name the repository
Risk if not fixed: Access to production code and deployment permissions could stay in place for people who no longer need it
Pattern or one-off: One-off in the evidence; the cause could repeat
Severity rationale: Partial compensating controls: the Q2 review covered the repository, and the analyst's check of the repository user list on 2026-10-14 found no former employees. Not High because no inappropriate access was found
Recommended remediation: Add a system checklist naming all four systems to the access review procedure. Run an out-of-cycle review of all four systems with user lists attached
Retest plan: Inspect the out-of-cycle review ticket and the four attached user lists, 2026-12-21 to 2026-12-23

Condition: One new account was created at 14:05 on 2026-06-18 and approved the next morning at 09:12. The other 37 accounts were approved first
Root cause: HR asked IT to create the account on the new hire's start day and the manager approved the ticket afterwards
Risk if not fixed: A user could briefly hold access that nobody accountable had approved
Severity rationale: The role was standard application access with no production data access, and the approval was recorded within 19 hours. No effect on the control objective
Recommended remediation: Require an approved ticket before account creation. Allow a pre-approval step for urgent starts so the approval still comes first
Retest plan: Check the next quarter's new accounts for approval order at the Q1 2027 follow-up

Condition: 2 of 16 terminated employees (12.5%) kept active accounts for 3 and 2 business days after their last working day. The limit is one business day
Root cause: HR's email notice reached IT after the last working day in both cases. The notice is an email with no ticket and no deadline
Risk if not fixed: A former employee could use company systems after leaving. A longer delay in the audit window would be a repeat exception
Severity rationale: The failure repeated with one cause and the control has no automatic trigger. No sign-in after the last working day was found, so Critical is not used
Recommended remediation: Create an automatic ticket from the HR system on the day a termination is entered, due one business day after the last working day. Review all termination accounts for the next 90 days as a stopgap
Remediation owner: IT Manager (with People Operations Lead for the HR system change)
Retest plan: Test all terminations from 2026-10-01 to 2026-12-11 in the 2026-12-14 to 2026-12-23 retest window

Condition: MFA was switched off for the production cloud console for about 71 hours (2026-06-03 10:20 to 2026-06-06 09:45). 9 sign-ins by 4 users occurred, 2 with a password only
Root cause: The setting was changed directly in the console during a migration task with no change ticket. No alert fires when an MFA policy changes. The lapse was found only by this test, about four months later
Risk if not fixed: A stolen password alone could have given access to the production environment, and nobody would have been told
Pattern or one-off: One-off event; the missing alert means it could recur unseen
Severity rationale: Production access was exposed with a single factor and nothing in place would have caught it. Both password-only users were enrolled in MFA and no misuse was found, but severity is set by what was exposed, as test plan section 8 says
Recommended remediation: Alert the security team on any change to MFA or sign-in policies in the identity provider, cloud console and code repository. Require a change ticket for policy changes. Add a guardrail so the console MFA requirement cannot be turned off without approval
Retest plan: Make a controlled test change to a sign-in policy and inspect the alert and ticket, in the 2026-12-14 to 2026-12-23 retest window

Condition: 2 of 40 randomly sampled changes (5%) reached production without independent review before release, both through the repository admin bypass. Separately, 1 of 9 emergency changes was reviewed 7 business days late, against a limit of 2
Root cause: Five administrators can bypass approval and no alert fires when they do. There is no backup reviewer rule for emergency changes
Pattern or one-off: Pattern for the bypass; separate cause for the emergency review
Severity rationale: The bypass is open to five people and unmonitored. The two changes were low risk (an email wording change and a reporting query fix) and no customer impact was found, so Critical is not used
Recommended remediation: Remove the bypass or limit it to a break-glass account that raises an alert. Name a backup reviewer for emergency changes. Add an automatic review reminder at day 2
Retest plan: Test all changes from 2026-10-01 to 2026-12-11 for the bypass, and all emergency changes for review timing, in the 2026-12-14 to 2026-12-23 retest window

Condition: Changes made directly in the production cloud console create no change record and need no approval. The control covers code deployments only
Root cause: The change control process and the pipeline cover code, and no rule covers console changes
Risk if not fixed: Production settings can be changed with no record, approval or review. D-04 was an example
Severity rationale: The cloud audit log records every console action, so changes can be found after the fact, but nobody reviews it. Critical was considered and not used for that reason. The exposure that actually occurred is rated once, in D-04
Recommended remediation: Extend change management to console changes, with a ticket required. Restrict console write access to a small group. Review the cloud audit log for console changes weekly
Retest plan: Inspect the updated procedure, the access list and two weekly log reviews, in the 2026-12-14 to 2026-12-23 retest window

Condition: 3 of 25 sampled findings (12%) were fixed after their deadline by 4, 9 and 14 days. Across all 138 findings, 17 (12%) were late or still open past the deadline on 2026-09-30, and 4 of those were Critical. No risk acceptance exists for any of them
Root cause: All three sampled findings are on the legacy reporting service. Its upgrades need downtime and no maintenance window was scheduled. The policy has no route for formally accepting a risk
Risk if not fixed: Known weaknesses stay open past the company's own deadlines
Severity rationale: The failure repeated, includes Critical findings and has no recorded decision behind it. Scanning itself worked in all 5 sampled runs
Recommended remediation: Schedule a maintenance window for the legacy reporting service. Close or formally accept the 17 overdue findings. Add a risk acceptance route to the policy with an approver and an expiry date
Remediation owner: Head of Security (with Engineering Lead for the maintenance window)
Retest plan: Re-run the deadline check on all findings detected from 2026-10-01 to 2026-12-11, and inspect the risk acceptance route, in the 2026-12-14 to 2026-12-23 retest window

Condition: 1 of 40 sampled alerts was closed with the single word dup and no link to the original alert. The extension of 25 more alerts had no exception
Root cause: The closing screen accepts any text as a note and has no required field for the original alert on a duplicate
Risk if not fixed: A real alert could be closed as a duplicate with no way to check it
Severity rationale: The alert was a true duplicate of one triaged 20 minutes earlier, so no event was missed, and the extended sample was clean. Alert rules for policy changes are rated under D-04
Recommended remediation: Make the original alert link a required field when an alert is closed as a duplicate
Retest plan: Check duplicate closures in Q1 2027 at the follow-up

Condition: 1 of 25 sampled backup jobs failed and was re-run 2 business days later, against a limit of 1. The extension of 25 more jobs had no exception
Root cause: Failure notices go to a shared mailbox with no assigned reader. The on-time re-runs happened because an engineer happened to check the backup dashboard
Risk if not fixed: A backup failure could go unnoticed for days, which would weaken recovery
Pattern or one-off: One-off in the evidence; the cause could repeat
Severity rationale: The annual restore test passed (3 hours 10 minutes against 4 hours) and 179 of 183 jobs succeeded, so recovery was not affected. The unmonitored mailbox is a partial gap, not a failure of the objective
Recommended remediation: Send failure notices to an on-call queue that creates a ticket with a due time. Assign a named reader. Extend the yearly restore test to customer upload storage and the analytics warehouse
Retest plan: Trigger a test failure and inspect the ticket and re-run time, 2026-12-21 to 2026-12-23. Schedule the extra restore tests before 2027-06-30

Condition: A critical vendor (V-09, document signing service) was onboarded without a risk review. The review is dated 2026-10-16, after the contract started on 2026-07-20 and after the analyst asked for it
Root cause: The contract was signed from a business request without the vendor review step, and nothing blocks signature until a review is approved
Risk if not fixed: Third parties could handle company data with no check
Pattern or one-off: Pattern risk; 1 of 2 onboardings in the period
Severity rationale: The vendor holds a current SOC 2 Type II report and the late review rated the risk low, which is a partial compensating control. The missing gate before signature means it could repeat
Recommended remediation: Require an approved vendor review before contract signature. Add a next-review-due field to the vendor register. Review all vendors onboarded in the last 12 months again to confirm no other gaps
Retest plan: Inspect the signature gate and the register, then test any vendor onboarded from 2026-10-01 to 2026-12-18, 2026-12-21 to 2026-12-23

Condition: The yearly review for V-08 (source code hosting provider) was done on time, 359 days after the prior review, but the record was not produced by the evidence deadline of 2026-10-12. It arrived on 2026-10-19
Root cause: The review file was kept outside the vendor register and the owner could not find it by the deadline
Risk if not fixed: The company could not prove a completed review when asked, for example by an auditor
Severity rationale: The review itself happened on time, so the control objective was met. The Not effective conclusion for CP-11 comes from the test plan rule on missing evidence, and severity measures impact, so the two differ
Recommended remediation: Store every review record in the vendor register so it can be produced on request
Retest plan: Retrieve three reviews from the register at the Q1 2027 follow-up

Condition: 2 of 25 sampled new hires (8%) finished training 42 and 49 days after their start date, against a limit of 30. Across all 38 new hires, 5 (13%) were late. The annual training passed for 25 of 25
Root cause: The course is assigned when the HR record is created, and in all late cases the record was entered more than 7 days after the start date
Risk if not fixed: New employees work with company systems without knowing security rules for longer than the policy allows
Severity rationale: No exposure was found and the annual training was complete. The delay is limited to a few weeks and has a clear, single cause
Recommended remediation: Assign the course automatically on the start date. Require HR records to be created by the start date and track exceptions weekly
Retest plan: Test all new hires who started from 2026-10-01 to 2026-11-15 for completion within 30 days, 2026-12-21 to 2026-12-23
